<div class="eyebrow">The problem</div>

## Small data, long job {background-image="assets/slide-frame.png" background-size="contain" background-color="white"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">The problem</div>
```

Nothing here is a big data problem. It is the same small data, over and over

```{=html}
<div class="equation">
  <p>
    <span class="fragment"><span class="num">10</span> re-samples</span>
    <span class="fragment"> <span class="times">x</span> <span class="num">100</span> combinations</span>
    <span class="fragment"> = <span class="num">1,000</span> model fits and evaluations</span>
  </p>
</div>
```

:::{.fragment .centered}
It's a "big processing" problem
:::

# Run the same code in Spark {.dark-slide background-image="assets/slide-frame-dark.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#031042"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">Removing the barrier</div>
```

## One function does everything{background-image="assets/slide-frame.png" background-size="contain" background-color="white"}

The new `tune_grid_spark()` function does the following:

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">Removing the barrier</div>
```

![](assets/sparklyr.png){.absolute top=0 left=1153 width=94}

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div class="step s-blue fragment">
    <div class="chev"><span class="num">01</span></div>
    <h3>Uploads</h3>
    <p><b>Re-samples</b>, <b>model</b> and <b>recipe</b> objects are transmitted to Spark</p>
  </div>
  <div class="step s-magenta fragment">
    <div class="chev"><span class="num">02</span></div>
    <h3>Tunes in Spark</h3>
    <p>Every combination is fitted on a Spark task, and in real R</p>
  </div>
  <div class="step s-green fragment">
    <div class="chev"><span class="num">03</span></div>
    <h3>Collects</h3>
    <p>Results from Spark are compiled into a <code>tune_results</code> object</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## One new argument {background-image="assets/slide-frame.png" background-size="contain" background-color="white"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">Removing the barrier</div>
```

![](assets/sparklyr.png){.absolute top=0 left=1153 width=94}

:::{.lead}
Adding `sc` is the only change, and the result is a regular `tune_results` object.
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="46%"}
[Locally]{.col-label}

:::{.sample-tiny}
```r
tune_grid(
  object = spec_bt,
  preprocessor = recipe_basic,
  resamples = readmission_folds,
  grid = bt_grid,
  control = control_grid()
)
```
:::
:::

::: {.column width="54%"}
[On Databricks]{.col-label}

:::{.sample-tiny}
```{.r code-line-numbers="|1|2|"}
tune_grid_spark(
  sc = sc,
  object = spec_bt,
  preprocessor = recipe_basic,
  resamples = readmission_folds,
  grid = bt_grid,
  control = control_grid()
)
```
:::
:::

::::


## The R packages {background-image="assets/slide-frame.png" background-size="contain" background-color="white"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">Removing the barrier</div>
```

![](assets/brickster.png){.absolute top=0 left=1153 width=94}

:::{.lead}
Scripted with `brickster`, or by hand in the cluster's Libraries tab.
:::

:::{.sample-small}
```r
repo <- "https://databricks.packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/noble/latest"

r_libs <- libraries(
  lib_cran("reticulate", repo = repo),
  lib_cran("tidymodels", repo = repo),
  lib_cran("xgboost", repo = repo),
  lib_cran("readmission", repo = repo)
)
db_libs_install(cluster_id, r_libs)
```
:::

## The Python package {background-image="assets/slide-frame.png" background-size="contain" background-color="white"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">Removing the barrier</div>
```

![](assets/brickster.png){.absolute top=0 left=1153 width=94}

:::{.lead}
`rpy2` is what lets the workers run real R. Install it once, then wait.
:::

:::{.sample-small}
```r
py_lib <- lib_pypi("rpy2==3.5.7") |>
  libraries()

db_libs_install(cluster_id, py_lib)

wait_for_lib_installs(cluster_id)
```
:::

# Hospital readmissions {.dark-slide background-image="assets/slide-frame-dark.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#031042"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">The example</div>
```

## Splitting the data {background-image="assets/slide-frame.png" background-size="contain" background-color="white"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">The example</div>
```

![](assets/tidymodels.png){.absolute top=0 left=1153 width=94}

:::{.lead}
Split for training and testing, and ten folds for cross validation.
:::

:::{.sample-small}
```r
library(tidymodels)
library(readmission)

set.seed(231)

readmission_splits <- initial_split(readmission, strata = readmitted)

readmission_folds <- vfold_cv(data   = training(readmission_splits), 
                              strata = readmitted)
```
:::

## The recipe {background-image="assets/slide-frame.png" background-size="contain" background-color="white"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">The example</div>
```

![](assets/tidymodels.png){.absolute top=0 left=1153 width=94}

:::{.lead}
A recipe with 5 steps.
:::

:::{.sample-small}
```r
recipe_basic <- recipe(readmitted ~ ., data = training(readmission_splits)) |>
  step_mutate(
    race = factor(case_when(
      !(race %in% c("Caucasian", "African American")) ~ "Other",
      .default = race
    ))
  ) |>
  step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_YeoJohnson(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())
```
:::

## The model {background-image="assets/slide-frame.png" background-size="contain" background-color="white"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">The example</div>
```

![](assets/tidymodels.png){.absolute top=0 left=1153 width=94}

:::{.lead}
A boosted tree with four parameters to tune.
:::

:::{.sample-small}
```r
spec_bt <- boost_tree(
  mode = "classification",
  trees = 500,
  mtry = tune(),
  min_n = tune(),
  learn_rate = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune()
)
```
:::

## The grid {background-image="assets/slide-frame.png" background-size="contain" background-color="white"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">The example</div>
```

![](assets/tidymodels.png){.absolute top=0 left=1153 width=94}

:::{.lead}
100 combinations, spread evenly across the parameter space.
:::

:::{.sample-small}
```r
bt_grid <- grid_space_filling(
  mtry(range = c(5, 20)),
  min_n(),
  learn_rate(),
  tree_depth(),
  size = 100
)
```
:::

## Tuning locally {background-image="assets/slide-frame.png" background-size="contain" background-color="white"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">The example</div>
```

![](assets/tidymodels.png){.absolute top=0 left=1153 width=94}

:::{.lead}
An M3 laptop takes **11 minutes**. A Windows machine takes **61**.
:::

:::{.sample-small}
```r
library(future)
plan(multisession)

local_results <- tune_grid(
  object = spec_bt,
  preprocessor = recipe_basic,
  resamples = readmission_folds,
  grid = bt_grid,
  control = control_grid()
)
```
:::

  <div class="row"><div class="label">Spark, 10 concurrent</div><div class="bar fast" style="width:35px"></div><div class="time">5 min</div></div>

## What the numbers say {background-image="assets/slide-frame.png" background-size="contain" background-color="white"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">The payoff</div>
```

- **32x faster** than the same job on Posit Workbench, **4x faster** than the best laptop

- Concurrency is a dial: 10 workers gave 5 minutes, 32 gave 2.8

- An overnight job becomes a job you wait for

- Large grid searches at scale, with no refactoring

# What this is, and what it is not. {.dark-slide background-image="assets/slide-frame-dark.png" background-size="contain" background-color="#031042"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">Knowing the limits</div>
```

## Limitations {background-image="assets/slide-frame.png" background-size="contain" background-color="white"}

```{=html}
<div class="eyebrow">Limits</div>
```

:::{.incremental}
- The goal is to speed up the **search**, not to process big data. The data still has to fit in memory

- Results can differ slightly from local runs, because the OS, the R version and the package versions differ

- Downloading predictions roughly doubles the data moved across the wire

- If your data is larger than local memory, reach for Spark ML instead
:::
